chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: The Blue Flame and boogie-woogie player Bear Tracks
summary: Joe Ketchum's Blue Flame club, and the barefoot boogie-woogie pianist Bear Tracks he later wrote a song about.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And then they had the Blue Flame, which was run by a very popular guy around home named Joe Ketchum(?). Now, that was... He named it after Woody Herman's theme song, "Blue Flame," when Woody first came out... Was it Herman or Shaw? Which one was "Blue Flame"? I think it was Artie Shaw, and "The Blue Flame" was his theme song during that time. Anyway, it was one of the clarinet players. And he named this place after that. And it was a really nice place, you know, really nice, but it was still over there in all this, you know, dirt roads and mud when it rained... We had some great times playing in there, too. It was kind of classy.

There was a fellow who used to come through.... I've got to mention this fellow, because I wrote a song about him, and I recorded it on my album that I made, Feelings, on Muse Records. They used to call him Bear Tracks. And he would go around with these overalls on, and he'd be barefooted all the time. And he'd walk up through this mud, you know, and you could see where he's been because he's barefoot -- everybody called him "Bear Tracks," you know. And he'd go from place to place. And the minute that you'd take a break, or intermission, he would sit down to the piano and play the Boogie-Woogie, you know. He was a good Boogie-Woogie player. And he never had anything to say to
anybody; he'd just come in and play, and go to the next place. You know, never woof anybody or anything. But everybody knew Bear Tracks.
